audit_findings.title: Perpetual growth may be incompatible with a depleting reserve base and 1.5% reinvestment returns
audit_findings.magnitude: terminal value is a computed $191.7 million-$310.5 million, or 46.3%-50.9% of operating value; 2.5% growth at 1.5% RONTA requires reinvestment equal to 166.7% of owner earnings
audit_findings.mechanism: The terminal growth and reinvestment assumptions directly determine terminal OE and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Unless HighPeak Energy conducts successful ongoing exploration and development activities or continually acquires properties containing proved reserves, proved reserves will decline as those reserves are produced.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated model inconsistency, not merely a possible operating risk. A 1.5% return cannot support 2.5% perpetual OE growth from internally retained OE because the required reinvestment exceeds the OE generated. Reserve depletion strengthens the problem. Because almost half of operating value comes from the terminal period, correcting the inconsistency could reasonably change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Rerun the valuation with explicit production decline, reserve-replacement capital and acquisition economics; permit terminal growth only where incremental returns and funding support it, and include a finite-life or zero-growth case.

audit_findings.title: The existing common-equity claim may not survive the 2026 covenant reset unchanged
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.200 billion debt versus $146.346 million cash, a computed $1.053654 billion cash shortfall if accelerated; debt equals 173.2% of the $693 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: A covenant-driven restructuring, asset sale or refinancing would change equity-level interest expense, operating assets, cash and potentially the share denominator.
audit_findings.evidence: If such amounts were accelerated and became immediately due and payable, the Company does not expect it would have sufficient liquidity to repay such indebtedness and would likely need to pursue a restructuring, refinancing or other strategic alternatives, which may not be available on acceptable terms or at all.
audit_findings.explanation: No default is demonstrated: the company reported compliance at June 30, 2026 after obtaining another one-quarter covenant amendment. However, the repeated amendment and disclosed uncertainty when stricter covenants return in the third quarter establish an unresolved discontinuity that is plainly material. Acceleration could not be met with existing cash, while an asset sale, expensive refinancing or equity issuance could invalidate both the projected OE stream and current ownership claim.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the third-quarter 2026 covenant calculations and compliance certificate plus subsequent amendments, waivers, refinancing, asset-sale and ATM issuance records; then update interest expense, assets, cash and fully diluted shares and rerun every scenario.

audit_findings.title: The FY2025 anchor may capitalize temporary derivative gains
audit_findings.magnitude: $30.8 million noncash mark-to-market gain and $14.1 million cash settlements, totaling $44.9 million versus the $38.9 million OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Any unpurged mark-to-market gain inflates anchor OE; projecting finite cash hedge settlements beyond their contractual periods inflates future OE and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: During the year ended December 31, 2025, the Company recognized a net derivative gain of $44.9 million, including a $30.8 million mark-to-market gain and $14.1 million in net monthly settlement receipts.
audit_findings.explanation: The filed derivative amounts are material, but the supplied record does not show the FY2025 OE bridge, so inclusion in the $38.9 million anchor is not demonstrated. The noncash gain equals 79.2% of the anchor and must be excluded if present. Cash settlements are genuine 2025 cash flow but cannot be treated as perpetual because the disclosed hedge book is finite.
audit_findings.action: Trace the anchor line by line to verify removal of the $30.8 million mark-to-market gain; separately model the $14.1 million settlement component only through the hedge contracts' lives, followed by normalized unhedged economics, and rerun if either was compounded.

audit_findings.title: A long-term minimum-volume commitment can become an unmodeled operating claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $107.7 million maximum remaining commitment at 2026-06-30 if no further volumes are delivered; actual deliveries were 32,022 Bopd versus the 23,500 Bopd minimum
audit_findings.mechanism: Future delivery shortfalls would reduce OE through deficiency payments or market purchases; any unavoidable unfunded amount could also operate as a claim ahead of equity.
audit_findings.evidence: The remaining monetary commitment as of December 31, 2025, if the Company never delivers any additional volumes under the agreement, is approximately $115.9 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The obligation is active, but no current shortfall is demonstrated. Latest filed deliveries exceeded the minimum by 8,522 Bopd, or 36.3%, and banked credits may provide further protection. The $107.7 million figure is a zero-delivery maximum, not an expected liability. The risk should therefore be monitored as production declines or drilling is curtailed rather than charged immediately to value.
audit_findings.action: Update banked-dollar credits and forecast gross piped volumes, escalation rates, deficiency fees and replacement-purchase costs under each scenario; rerun OE only for forecast shortfalls not already captured in throughput expenses.

audit_findings.title: The latest-year anchor includes a material nonrecurring tax benefit unless specifically normalized
audit_findings.magnitude: $10.0 million, equal to 25.7% of the $38.9 million OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: If retained in normalized OE, the severance-tax refund raises the anchor and is compounded through explicit forecasts and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Production taxes per Boe for the year ended December 31, 2025, compared with 2024, decreased primarily due to the 20% overall decrease in realized sales prices and 3% decrease in average daily sales volumes in addition to a $10.0 million natural gas severance tax refund that was realized by taking advantage of previously unrealized marketing deductions allowed by the State of Texas.
audit_findings.explanation: The $10.0 million multi-year refund is filed and clearly nonrecurring, but its inclusion in the OE anchor is not demonstrated because no OE bridge was supplied. The amount remained recorded as a receivable at June 30, 2026, which is especially relevant if OE was derived from cash flows. If included, its scale is sufficient to affect value materially.
audit_findings.action: Trace the production-tax expense, refund receivable and operating-cash-flow adjustments into the FY2025 OE bridge; remove the one-time $10.0 million benefit while retaining only documented recurring marketing deductions, then rerun all scenarios if necessary.

audit_findings.title: Asset-retirement obligations may be omitted from both OE and the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $16.659 million recognized ARO at 2026-06-30, computed as $0.12 per fully diluted share and 2.2%-3.0% of scenario equity values
audit_findings.mechanism: Unfunded plugging and remediation spending belongs once in maintenance capital/OE or, if not forecast, as an equity-bridge deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company’s asset retirement obligations primarily relate to the future plugging and abandonment of wells and remediation of related facilities.
audit_findings.explanation: The record does not establish whether abandonment cash costs are already included in maintenance capital, so omission remains possible. Nevertheless, deducting the entire latest recognized liability would reduce value by only about $0.12 per share, leaving every scenario well below the $8.05 market price and not changing the valuation conclusion. Additional obligations beyond the recognized liability are unquantified.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile forecast plugging and remediation payments to maintenance capital and OE. If absent, deduct the $16.659 million recognized obligation once and verify that no amount is double-counted.
